units.source_text: 相信狗是“死神的使者”的原因是很单纯的。

en.t: The reason people believed dogs were messengers of the god of death was very simple.

units.source_text: 狗用令人毛骨悚然的吠声，来表达它凭嗅觉所感到的不安。

en.t: With a hair-raising bark, a dog expresses the uneasiness it senses through smell.

units.source_text: 弥留之际的病人越接近死亡，无疑就越会发出一种异样的臭味。

en.t: The closer a dying patient comes to death, the more surely he gives off a strange odor.

units.source_text: 特别是患热病的人更加厉害。

en.t: This is especially severe in people suffering from feverish illness.
The smell of a corpse is fouler still.

units.source_text: 临死前后也难怪狗要吠吼不止。

en.t: So it is no wonder that dogs keep barking and howling around the time of death.

units.source_text: 再说遇上一个人的死，这种臭味一度渗入鼻子，第二次再遇上，比前次更觉难以忍受，这是很自然的。

en.t: Besides, once this smell has seeped into the nose at someone's death, it is only natural that meeting it a second time feels even harder to endure than before.

units.source_text: 镇上的人是不是知道这种情况呢。

en.t: Did the people of the town know this?

units.source_text: 他们一度在某个死了人的人家看见狗，就像遇见恶魔般害怕，决定要把它杀掉。

en.t: Once they saw a dog at a house where someone had died, they were as frightened as if they had met a demon and decided to kill it.

units.source_text: 虽然不知道从前是谁说出“死神的御使”这句话，不过凶猛的热病一流行，镇上的狗群就会吠叫起来，使镇上本来的恐怖景象更增加了昏暗。

en.t: Although no one knows who first used the phrase "messenger of the god of death," whenever a fierce fever epidemic spread, the town's dogs would begin barking, making the town's already terrifying scene still darker.
